entry.title: The Pipes Model for Latency and Throughput Analysis
entry.summary:
In much of the distributed computing literature, latency is expressed as the number of communication rounds or network delays; such metrics do not directly account for the amount of data sent or the dependencies among parties sending the data. Throughput is also normally evaluated empirically. As a consequence, the standard models used for analysing state machine replication (SMR) protocols do not by themselves provide an end-to-end analytical comparison of practical latency and throughput as functions of per-processor bandwidth and transaction arrival rate.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #distributed-systems

entry.title: Ideal Pseudorandom Code, Revisited
entry.summary:
Pseudorandom error-correcting codes (PRCs), introduced by Christ and Gunn at CRYPTO’24, combine pseudorandomness with error correction, providing a natural abstraction for robust watermarking and steganography on generative AI models. Subsequent standalone notions, which are ideal security for secret-key PRCs and CCA-style security for public-key PRCs, are oracle-based and do not capture composable use with explicit parties, sessions, and corruption. We give a UC treatment of PRCs via corruption-aware ideal functionalities for both settings.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #compilers #combinatorics

entry.title: Toward Eﬃcient Post-Quantum Bitcoin Bridges. BitVM-style protocols verify succinct proofs on Bitcoin by garbling a proof veriﬁer oﬀ-chain.
entry.summary:
BitVM-style protocols verify succinct proofs on Bitcoin by garbling a proof veriﬁer oﬀ-chain. What reaches the chain in a dispute is the proof itself: its bits under one-time keys, the scripts that authenticate them and the signatures that bind them to transactions. Existing designs garble elliptic-curve succinct non-interactive argument of knowledge (SNARK) veriﬁers, which a quantum adversary breaks.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #post-quantum #consensus

entry.title: Extending the Schur--Macaulay Framework for UOV Attacks via Truncated Polynomial Algebras
entry.summary:
Building on the ideal-inclusion framework of Ding, Li, and Tao, we reformulate and extend the Schur--Macaulay approach of Merz and Ran using multigraded $p$-truncated polynomial algebras over arbitrary finite fields. The construction admits a reconciliation interpretation involving multiple oil vectors. Combining divided powers with transfer relation spaces, we derive quotient-dimension criteria for recovering graded components of the hidden oil-space ideal.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp

entry.title: Shuffling is Universal: Statistical Additive Randomized Encodings for All Functions
entry.summary:
The shuffle model is a widely used abstraction for non-interactive anonymous communication. It allows $n$ parties holding private inputs $x_1,\dots,x_n$ to simultaneously send messages to an evaluator, so that the messages are received in a random order. The evaluator can then compute a joint function $f(x_1,\dots,x_n)$, ideally while learning nothing else about the private inputs.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #rust #combinatorics

entry.title: Vectorised Hashing Based on Bernstein-Rabin-Winograd Polynomials over Prime Order Fields
entry.summary:
We introduce the new AXU hash function decBRWHash, which is parameterised by the positive integer $c$ and is based on Bernstein-Rabin-Winograd (BRW) polynomials. Choosing $c>1$ gives a hash function which can be implemented using $c$-way single instruction multiple data (SIMD) instructions. We report a set of very comprehensive hand optimised assembly implementations of 4-decBRWHash using avx2 SIMD instructions available on modern Intel processors.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #number-theory

entry.title: Connecting Cryptanalytic Distinguishers through Divisibility
entry.summary:
Integral distinguishers can reveal more than a zero-sum property: the number of ones in an output component may be divisible by a high power of $2$, rather than merely being even. To exploit this divisibility, we relate linear, integral, differential-linear, and restricted differential sums through two-way conversions with explicit divisibility guarantees and data complexity, recovering established links as special cases. We derive exact random-permutation probabilities and rigorous bounds to quantify the distinguishing strength while accounting for dependencies between output conditions.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #infosec
